scope: Source-level lesson mapping only; no linguistic, audio, runtime, native, or release approval

spanish.title: Greetings and clear vowels
spanish.objective: Greetings and clear vowels: Say each Spanish vowel clearly: a, e, i, o, u.

japanese.title: Hello and your name
japanese.focus: Hear the five Japanese vowels あ・い・う・え・お. Use a polite greeting and ～です for a name; は marks the topic and is pronounced wa here. Add か at the end to make a polite question.

french.title: Greetings and your name
french.objective: Greet a new adult learner, exchange names politely, and hear and produce the French /ʒ/, /u/, and nasal /ɔ̃/ sounds in familiar words.
french.focus: Greet someone with bonjour and introduce yourself with je m’appelle. The j in je and bonjour sounds /ʒ/; ou in bonjour sounds /u/; on in bonjour is a nasal vowel /ɔ̃/ with no separate n sound. Some final consonants are silent (Paris, salut), but others are pronounced (Marc, Paul, bonjour). Use vous with an adult you have just met; save tu for familiar classmates once you agree to be informal. A woman writes enchantée with a final -e; it sounds the same as enchanté.

spanish.title: El, la, un and una
spanish.objective: El, la, un and una: A noun has grammatical gender.

japanese.title: This and that
japanese.focus: Practice hiragana in short nouns. これ is this (near me), それ is that (near you), and あれ is that over there. この goes before a noun; の connects nouns or marks possession. Japanese nouns have no articles or grammatical gender.

french.title: Masculine and feminine: le, la, un, une
french.objective: Name familiar classroom objects with un or une, and use le or la when pointing to a specific object.
french.focus: French nouns are grammatically masculine or feminine. Learn each object with its article: un stylo, une trousse. Use un/une when naming or introducing one object (C’est un cahier); use le/la for a particular object already identified (Voilà la gomme). The noun ending is only a partial gender clue, so learn the article with the noun. Hear the difference between nasal un and pronounced n in une, and between le and la.

spanish.title: One thing or several
spanish.objective: One thing or several: Usually add -s after a vowel and -es after a consonant.

japanese.title: One or several
japanese.focus: Keep practicing hiragana and recognize katakana in loanwords (ノート, ゴム). Japanese nouns usually do not change for plural; quantity and context tell us how many. Use ～つ for general items such as erasers; bound notebooks use ～さつ (にさつ means two notebooks). The object particle を is pronounced o. も means also or too and replaces は or を.

french.title: One thing or several: des, les and plurals
french.objective: Distinguish one classroom object from several using un/une/des and le/la/les, and hear plural meaning through the article.
french.focus: Most French plurals are written with -s: un crayon → des crayons. The final -s is usually silent, so the article often tells you whether one or several are meant: le /lə/ versus les /le/, un or une versus des /de/. Un and une become des for unspecified plural objects; le and la become les for specific plural objects. Nouns already ending in -s, -x, or -z keep that ending in the plural. Other patterns come later; learn each new plural in context.

spanish.title: Who is speaking?
spanish.objective: Who is speaking?: Yo means I, tú means informal you, and usted means formal you.

japanese.title: Who is speaking?
japanese.focus: Use a name or わたし when needed, but notice that Japanese often omits a subject clear from context. Ask どなたですか politely for who; だれですか is less formal. Use ～さん politely after a person's name.

french.title: Who is speaking?
french.objective: Introduce yourself and a classmate with je suis, tu es, and nous sommes; identify a third person or group with il/elle est or ils/elles sont, keeping tu or vous consistent with the relationship.
french.focus: Use être for “am / is / are”: je suis, tu es, il/elle est, nous sommes, vous êtes, ils/elles sont. Peers often use tu right away; use vous with a teacher, staff member, or an adult stranger, and keep one register in a conversation. A mixed group uses ils, and masculine plural étudiants; an all-female group uses elles and étudiantes. In est the final t is usually silent, but it links before a vowel in il est ici; the t in êtes is pronounced.

spanish.title: Ser: identity and origin
spanish.objective: Ser: identity and origin: Use ser for identity, origin and characteristics.

japanese.title: Identity and origin
japanese.focus: Use ～です for identity or role and ～から きました for where someone came from. は introduces the topic; が can identify the person answering who, but keep the contrast contextual.

french.title: Who am I? Identity and origin
french.objective: Introduce a learner’s role and origin with être and the appropriate Je viens de country chunk, and describe a person with a correctly matched adjective.
french.focus: Use être for roles and traits: je suis étudiant or étudiante; il est gentil, elle est gentille. A role normally has no article after être: je suis étudiante. Learn the noun or adjective ending for the person described. Learn Je viens de as a fixed origin chunk for now: de France for a feminine country, d’Espagne before a vowel, du Canada for a masculine country, and des États-Unis for a plural country. Country articles matter; do not apply de to every country.

spanish.title: Estar: location and condition
spanish.objective: Estar: location and condition: Use estar for a person's or object's location and for conditions.

japanese.title: Where people and things are
japanese.focus: Use あります for inanimate things and います for people or animals. に marks where something exists; ここ, そこ, and あそこ locate it.

french.title: Where is it? Location and state
french.objective: Locate a person or object with être, sur, dans, or près de/du, and describe a state with an adjective that matches the noun or person.
french.focus: Use être for the locations and states in this lesson: Le livre est sur la table; La porte est ouverte. Some other everyday states use avoir (for example, j’ai faim); those come later. Sur means on, dans means in, and près de means near; before le, de + le becomes du (près du livre), and before les it becomes des (here meaning de + les, distinct from the indefinite article des). For a thing, il replaces a masculine noun and elle a feminine noun: le livre → il, la trousse → elle. Adjectives agree with the noun or person: le livre est ouvert, la porte est ouverte; Marc est fatigué, Claire est fatiguée.

spanish.title: Hay: what exists
spanish.objective: Hay: what exists: Hay means there is or there are.

japanese.title: What is in the room?
japanese.focus: Ask ～に なにが ありますか about things and ～に だれが いますか about people. Reuse the あります/います contrast and location words without treating them as interchangeable.

french.title: Il y a: what exists
french.objective: Say what exists with il y a and where something is with être; negate existence with il n’y a pas de or d’ before a vowel.
french.focus: Il y a means there is or there are and does not change for number. Use est, a form of être, for where a particular thing is. In il n’y a pas de + noun, de replaces un, une or des; write d’ before a vowel: il n’y a pas d’ordinateur. Review la/une/les with noun gender and number.

spanish.title: Numbers and age
spanish.objective: Numbers and age: Use tener for age: tengo dieciocho años, literally I have eighteen years.

japanese.title: Numbers, age, and counters
japanese.focus: Read numbers one to ten. なんにん means how many people; いくつ means how many general items. Use ～さい（歳） for age and an appropriate counter for objects; ～つ counts general items, while ～にん（人） counts people. Some readings change, including ひとり（一人）. に (two) sounds the same as the location particle に; さん (three) sounds the same as the polite name suffix. 18 is じゅうはち, but 18 years old is じゅうはっさい.

french.title: Numbers and age
french.objective: Give an assigned age with avoir (j’ai dix-huit ans), count 1–20, and say how many students there are and how many books a class needs.
french.focus: French uses avoir for age: j’ai dix-huit ans, literally “I have eighteen years,” never je suis. Learn j’ai, tu as, il/elle a, nous avons; Tu as quel âge ? asks “How old are you?” Use il y a for a count and avoir besoin de + number + noun for a need. Count 1–20, including dix-huit and vingt. Pronunciation: dix is /dis/ alone, /di/ before a consonant, /diz/ before a vowel; dix-huit is /dizɥit/ and vingt ans links the final t. There is no elision before onze: de onze livres.

spanish.title: Simple questions and no
spanish.objective: Simple questions and no: Put no before the verb to make a negative.

japanese.title: Ask and say no
japanese.focus: Add か to make a polite question. Say いいえ for no and use じゃありません for a negative noun sentence (more formal: では ありません); polite verb negatives use ～ません.

french.title: Simple questions and no
french.objective: Ask simple yes/no questions in French and make a negative with ne…pas.
french.focus: Make a negative with ne before the verb and pas after it: je ne suis pas, je n’ai pas. Before a vowel or mute h, ne becomes n’: elle n’est pas, je n’ai pas. After a negated avoir, un/une/des usually become de: je n’ai pas de livre; after être, keep the article: ce n’est pas un livre. Ask yes/no questions with rising intonation (Tu as un livre ?) or est-ce que. In conversation ne is often dropped, but write the full ne…pas in this course. Être covers identity and location; avoir expresses possession. Je suis étudiant has no article before the role.

spanish.title: Ask for help and review
spanish.objective: Ask for help and review: Use a short repair phrase when you need help: No entiendo; ¿Puedes repetir?; Más despacio, por favor.

japanese.title: Ask for help and review
japanese.focus: Keep a conversation going with わかりません and もういちど おねがいします; the reply ゆっくり はなします means I will speak slowly. Review なんですか and ～が あります from Foundation.

french.title: Ask for help and review
french.objective: Ask a classmate to repeat or speak more slowly, ask a teacher politely, and review selected earlier forms: être, articles, agreement, il y a (from Lesson 7) and ne…pas.
french.focus: New repair phrases: Je ne comprends pas (ce mot); Tu peux répéter, s’il te plaît ?; Plus lentement, s’il te plaît. Use Vous pouvez répéter, s’il vous plaît ? with a teacher. Comprendre means to understand; répéter means to repeat; plus lentement means more slowly. Review être, articles, noun/adjective agreement, il y a from Lesson 7, and full ne…pas. With a plain role, say je suis étudiante without an article; when the role noun has an adjective, the article returns: je suis une nouvelle étudiante or je suis un nouvel étudiant. The adjective comes before the noun: nouveau before a masculine consonant, nouvel before a masculine vowel sound (un nouvel étudiant), and nouvelle for feminine (une nouvelle étudiante). Plus has a silent s in plus lentement. Keep the pronoun/verb in the chosen tu or vous register. Pronunciation: un étudiant links the n to the vowel; est-ce que sounds roughly “es-kuh”; the final consonants of comprends and pas are silent; il y a is pronounced together as a short group.

spanish.title: Regular -ar verbs
spanish.objective: Regular -ar verbs: Remove -ar and add -o, -as, -a, -amos, -an: hablo, hablas, habla, hablamos, hablan.

japanese.title: Polite verbs for everyday actions
japanese.focus: Practice polite ～ます forms for familiar actions; a time word such as あした can also make them describe a future action. で marks where an action happens (としょかんで はたらきます); と marks the person you do it with (ともだちと はなします), rather than linking two nouns as in Foundation.

french.title: Regular -er verbs
french.objective: Verbes réguliers en -er : retirer -er et ajouter -e, -es, -e, -ons, -ent : parle, parles, parle, parlons, parlent.
french.focus: Regular -er verbs (parler, étudier, travailler, écouter, pratiquer)

spanish.title: Regular -er verbs
spanish.objective: Regular -er verbs: Remove -er and add -o, -es, -e, -emos, -en: como, comes, come, comemos, comen.

japanese.title: Common verb groups
japanese.focus: Notice たべる→たべます (る-verb), のむ→のみます (う-verb), and irregular する→します and くる→きます. Learn each polite form in context.

french.title: Regular -er verbs, with irregular exceptions
french.objective: Verbes réguliers en -er : retirer -er et ajouter -e, -es, -e, -ons, -ent (manger : mange, manges, mange, mangeons, mangent). Boire, lire et comprendre sont irréguliers et se mémorisent à part.
french.focus: Regular -er verbs (manger), plus irregular boire, lire and comprendre

spanish.title: Regular -ir verbs
spanish.objective: Regular -ir verbs: Remove -ir and add -o, -es, -e, -imos, -en.

japanese.title: Polite past and negative
japanese.focus: Use ～ました for a completed action and ～ません for a polite negative. ～ませんでした says it did not happen.

french.title: Regular -ir verbs, with irregular exceptions
french.objective: Verbes réguliers en -ir : retirer -ir et ajouter -is, -is, -it, -issons, -issent (finir : finis, finis, finit, finissons, finissent). Vivre, écrire, ouvrir et recevoir sont irréguliers dans cette leçon.
french.focus: Regular -ir verbs (finir), plus irregular vivre, écrire, ouvrir and recevoir

spanish.title: Adjective agreement
spanish.objective: Adjective agreement: Adjectives agree with the noun they describe: un libro rojo, unas mochilas rojas.

japanese.title: Two kinds of adjective
japanese.focus: い-adjectives directly describe nouns. な-adjectives take な before a noun; neither agrees for gender or plural. きれい ends in い but is a な-adjective (きれいな へや).

french.title: Accord des adjectifs
french.objective: Accordez les adjectifs au genre et au nombre du nom : un sac rouge, des sacs rouges, une petite trousse, des petites trousses.
french.focus: Gender and number agreement for common descriptive adjectives

spanish.title: Mi, tu and su
spanish.objective: Mi, tu and su: Possessives agree with what is possessed, not the owner: mi libro, mis libros; tu mesa, tus mesas.

japanese.title: Whose item is it, and is it good?
japanese.focus: Review の for ownership while adding a polite negative い-adjective. Remove the final い and add くないです: おおきい → おおきくないです (not big). The common adjective いい is irregular: よくないです (not good). The くないです pattern works only for い-adjectives; な-adjectives such as しずか and きれい do not take it.

french.title: Mon, ton et son
french.objective: Choisissez mon, ton ou son selon le genre et le nombre de l'objet possédé, et non selon le propriétaire : mon cahier, ma table, mes livres.
french.focus: Possessive determiners mon/ma/mes, ton/ta/tes, son/sa/ses

spanish.title: Tener: possessions and needs
spanish.objective: Tener: possessions and needs: Tener is irregular: tengo, tienes, tiene, tenemos, tienen.

japanese.title: Have and need
japanese.focus: Use あります for possessing a thing in simple contexts. ～が ひつようです states that something is needed; ～が いります is conversational.

french.title: Avoir : possessions et besoins
french.objective: Utilisez avoir au présent pour exprimer ce que l'on possède et certains besoins : j'ai, tu as, il a, nous avons, ils ont ; j'ai faim, elle a soif.
french.focus: Present-tense avoir, possession, hunger and thirst

spanish.title: Ir and the contraction al
spanish.objective: Ir and the contraction al: Ir is voy, vas, va, vamos, van.

japanese.title: Go, come, and return
japanese.focus: いきます moves away, きます toward the speaker or reference point, and かえります returns home. に or へ marks a destination.

french.title: Aller et la contraction au
french.objective: Dites où vous allez avec aller au présent et choisissez au, à la, à l’ ou aux selon le lieu.
french.focus: Aller in the present; à + le = au, à + les = aux

spanish.title: Questions with qué and cuál
spanish.objective: Questions with qué and cuál: Qué asks what something is or what someone does.

japanese.title: What or which?
japanese.focus: なに asks what before particles such as を; なん is common before です. どれ stands alone for which one among several, and どの modifies a noun.

french.title: Poser des questions : que et quel
french.objective: Demandez ce que quelqu’un étudie et choisissez entre des cours ou des livres avec que, quel et lequel en contexte.
french.focus: Que/quoi for what; quel/quelle for which; lequel for which one

spanish.title: Where, when and why
spanish.objective: Where, when and why: Dónde asks where, cuándo asks when, and por qué asks why.

japanese.title: Where, when, and why
japanese.focus: Use どこ for where, いつ for when, and どうして for why. Answer with a short reason using ～から when appropriate; here から means because, unlike the from in そこから (lesson 7).

french.title: Où, quand et pourquoi
french.objective: Posez trois questions distinctes sur le lieu, le moment et la raison, puis répondez avec à, à neuf heures et parce que.
french.focus: Où, quand, pourquoi; répondre avec parce que

spanish.title: Time and schedules
spanish.objective: Time and schedules: Use es la una but son las dos, tres and so on.

japanese.title: Time and schedules
japanese.focus: Say a clock time with ～じ（時） and minutes with ～ふん/ぷん（分）. に marks a scheduled time; some number readings change before counters. ～ましょう suggests doing something together, while ～ましょうか asks the other person to decide.

french.title: Dire l’heure et organiser sa journée
french.objective: Dites l’heure avec il est, puis indiquez à quelle heure commencent et finissent les activités de la journée.
french.focus: Il est + heure; à + heure for schedules; du matin / de l’après-midi

spanish.title: Gustar: one thing or many
spanish.objective: Gustar: one thing or many: With gustar, the liked thing controls the verb: me gusta el libro; me gustan los libros.

japanese.title: Likes and dislikes
japanese.focus: すき (好き) and きらい (嫌い) express likes and dislikes; the item commonly takes が. They do not follow an English verb pattern.

french.title: Dire ce qu’on aime
french.objective: Exprimez vos goûts avec aimer au présent et distinguez j’aime, nous aimons, ils aiment et la négation.
french.focus: Aimer + noun or infinitive; French subject agreement and ne…pas

spanish.title: Querer: wants
spanish.objective: Querer: wants: Querer changes e to ie in quiero, quieres, quiere and quieren; nosotros queremos keeps e.

japanese.title: Wanting things and actions
japanese.focus: ～がほしい marks the wanted thing with が. ～たい attaches to a verb’s ます-stem (たべます → たべたい); its object often takes を, and が is also common. At a café, use ～をください to order.

french.title: Vouloir et les projets du samedi
french.objective: Dites ce que vous voulez faire avec vouloir au présent, suivi d’un infinitif, et comparez je veux, nous voulons et ils veulent.
french.focus: Vouloir present tense + infinitive; polite choice with je voudrais

spanish.title: Poder: ability and permission
spanish.objective: Poder: ability and permission: Poder changes o to ue except in nosotros: puedo, puedes, puede, podemos, pueden.

japanese.title: Can I? May I?
japanese.focus: できます states ability; verbs can also have potential forms such as よみます → よめます (can read). ～てもいいですか asks permission; ～てはいけません prohibits an action. Here とって is the て-form of とります; learn the two とって phrases together for now, then study the て-form in lesson 20.

french.title: Pouvoir : possibilité et permission
french.objective: Dites ce que vous pouvez faire et demandez poliment la permission dans une bibliothèque.
french.focus: pouvoir + infinitif : je peux, tu peux, il/elle peut, nous pouvons, ils/elles peuvent; est-ce que je peux… ?

spanish.title: Necesitar and tener que
spanish.objective: Necesitar and tener que: Necesitar + infinitive expresses a need.

japanese.title: What must be done
japanese.focus: Use ～なければなりません or conversational ～ないといけません for an obligation. Both say that something must be done. First make the plain negative: for う-verbs, change the last sound to the あ-row and add ない (いきます → いく → いかない; かいます, buy → かう → かわない, with final う becoming わ). For る-verbs, drop る and add ない (たべる → たべない). Irregular する → しない and くる → こない. Replace ない with なければなりません, or add といけません after ない.

french.title: Exprimer un besoin et une obligation
french.objective: Distinguez avoir besoin de pour un besoin et devoir pour une obligation avant un examen.
french.focus: avoir besoin de + nom/infinitif; devoir + infinitif : je dois, tu dois, il/elle doit, nous devons

spanish.title: Hacer and daily activities
spanish.objective: Hacer and daily activities: Hacer has the irregular yo form hago.

japanese.title: Doing everyday activities
japanese.focus: Many activities use a noun plus します, such as べんきょうします (study) and そうじします (clean). You may also hear noun + を + します.

french.title: Faire et les activités du quotidien
french.objective: Décrivez des tâches et habitudes avec faire et des verbes précis quand le français les préfère.
french.focus: faire : je fais, tu fais, il/elle fait, nous faisons, ils/elles font; faire du sport, faire ses devoirs

spanish.title: Reflexive routines
spanish.objective: Reflexive routines: A reflexive pronoun changes with the person: me, te, se, nos, se.

japanese.title: A daily routine in order
japanese.focus: Use time words, まず (first), それから (then), and さいごに (finally) to connect ordinary actions. Seven o’clock is read しちじ.

french.title: Les gestes du matin
french.objective: Racontez une routine avec les verbes pronominaux au présent et accordez le pronom avec la personne.
french.focus: se lever, se doucher, se préparer, se coucher, se réveiller; me, te, se, nous, vous, se

spanish.title: This, that and those
spanish.objective: This, that and those: Demonstratives agree with the noun: este libro, esta mesa, estos libros, estas mesas.

japanese.title: Prices and choices
japanese.focus: Use いくら to ask a price. ひゃく is one hundred, にひゃく is two hundred, and さんびゃく is three hundred (after さん, ひゃく changes to びゃく). えん means yen. For later prices, せん is one thousand, にせん is two thousand, and さんぜん is three thousand (せん changes to ぜん). Review これ/それ/あれ as standalone choices and この/その/あの before nouns.

french.title: Choisir ce livre ou celui-là
french.objective: Désignez des objets proches ou plus éloignés avec ce, cet, cette, ces et les pronoms celui ou celle.
french.focus: ce / cet / cette / ces + nom; celui / celle; -ci / -là for explicit contrast

spanish.title: Location prepositions
spanish.objective: Location prepositions: Use en for in/on/at as context requires.

japanese.title: Being somewhere and doing something there
japanese.focus: に marks a place where someone or something exists; で marks the place of an action. Use position nouns such as うえ (上), した (下), and なか (中) with の.

french.title: Trouver la salle de cours
french.objective: Donnez un itinéraire simple dans un bâtiment avec au, près de, loin de, sous, devant et derrière.
french.focus: au deuxième étage; près du café; loin de l’école; sous la table; devant / derrière

spanish.title: Future plans with ir a
spanish.objective: Future plans with ir a: Use a present form of ir + a + infinitive: voy a estudiar.

japanese.title: Plans for tomorrow
japanese.focus: Present polite forms can express future plans with a time word. ～つもりです states intention and ～よていです states a scheduled plan. Both follow the plain dictionary form (あいます → あう; します → する).

french.title: Prévoir demain
french.objective: Annoncez des projets proches avec aller au présent suivi d’un infinitif et posez une question sur le programme d’un ami.
french.focus: je vais, tu vas, il/elle va, nous allons, ils/elles vont + infinitif

spanish.title: Actions happening now
spanish.objective: Actions happening now: Use estar + gerund for an action in progress: estoy hablando.

japanese.title: What is happening now?
japanese.focus: ～ています can show an action in progress. It uses the て-form: よみます → よんで、のみます → のんで、まちます → まって. The form also includes します → して, as in なにを していますか. Some ～ています forms describe a resulting state instead; you will meet these later.

french.title: Ce qui se passe maintenant
french.objective: Décrivez une action en cours avec être en train de + infinitif et reconnaissez le présent simple lorsque le contexte suffit.
french.focus: être en train de + infinitif; je suis, tu es, il/elle est, nous sommes, ils/elles sont

spanish.title: Saber and conocer
spanish.objective: Saber and conocer: Use saber for a fact or an ability with an infinitive.

japanese.title: Know, understand, or be able to
japanese.focus: しっています (知っています) is a resulting ～ています state: someone knows after learning. しりません is its usual negative. わかります means understand; できます means can do. いけます is the potential of いきます (can go).

french.title: Savoir un fait, connaître une personne
french.objective: Choisissez savoir pour un fait ou une compétence et connaître pour une personne, un lieu ou une chose familière.
french.focus: savoir + fait/question/infinitif; connaître + personne/lieu

spanish.title: Comparisons
spanish.objective: Comparisons: Use más .

japanese.title: Compare useful choices
japanese.focus: A は B より… compares A with B. A と B と、どちらが… asks which of two; いちばん marks the top choice in a group.

french.title: Comparer deux lieux
french.objective: Comparez deux lieux d’étude avec plus, moins et aussi ; employez meilleur et mieux dans le bon contexte.
french.focus: plus/moins + adjectif + que; aussi + adjectif + que; meilleur pour + nom

spanish.title: Direct object pronouns
spanish.objective: Direct object pronouns: Lo, la, los and las replace a direct object and agree with it: el libro → lo; las llaves → las.

japanese.title: The object of an action
japanese.focus: を marks the direct object of many actions. Once the object is clear, Japanese can omit it naturally where English uses it or them. も can replace を when adding another object, as in ペンも いれます.

french.title: Remplacer ce qu’on cherche
french.objective: Remplacez un objet déjà nommé par le, la, l’ ou les et placez ce pronom avant le verbe conjugué.
french.focus: le, la, l’, les before a conjugated verb; object gender and number

spanish.title: Indirect objects: to whom?
spanish.objective: Indirect objects: to whom?: Me, te, le, nos and les can identify the recipient: le doy el libro a Ana.

japanese.title: Giving and receiving
japanese.focus: に marks the recipient with あげます and くれます. With もらいます, the giver takes に or から. The three verbs differ by whose perspective the sentence takes.

french.title: Dire à qui l’on donne
french.objective: Dites à qui s’adresse une action avec me, te, lui, nous ou leur devant le verbe.
french.focus: me, te, lui, nous, leur as indirect-object pronouns; à + recipient

spanish.title: Personal a
spanish.objective: Personal a: Use personal a before a specific person who is a direct object: veo a Ana.

japanese.title: People as objects or destinations
japanese.focus: Use に with あいます for the person you meet. To go to a person, say [person] の ところに いきます. Use を with よびます (call over) or てつだいます (help). The particle depends on the Japanese verb.

french.title: Chercher une personne
french.objective: Parlez de personnes et de choses que vous cherchez, voyez ou connaissez, sans ajouter de préposition devant le complément direct en français.
french.focus: verbe transitif + personne/chose; pas de « a » personnel en français

spanish.title: Regular completed past actions
spanish.objective: Regular completed past actions: The preterite reports completed past actions.

japanese.title: Invite someone and report back
japanese.focus: Use a polite negative question ～ませんか to invite someone: べんきょうしませんか asks “Would you like to study?” rather than stating that you do not study. Answer with a time or activity; use ～ました to report a completed action from yesterday.

french.title: Raconter hier
french.objective: Racontez des actions achevées hier au passé composé avec avoir et distinguez les participes réguliers de quelques formes fréquentes irrégulières.
french.focus: passé composé: avoir au présent + participe passé; -é/-i/-u and acheté, étudié, parlé, fini, mangé, écrit

spanish.title: Ir and ser in the past
spanish.objective: Ir and ser in the past: Fui, fuiste, fue, fuimos and fueron are preterite forms of both ir and ser.
spanish.focus: Ir and ser in the past

japanese.title: Polite past and what did not happen
japanese.focus: Contrast past statements with past negatives. For verbs, ～ます → ～ました, while ～ません → ～ませんでした. Nouns and な-adjectives use ～でした / ～ではありませんでした (りょこうでした → りょこうではありませんでした; きれいでした → きれいではありませんでした); for an い-adjective remove final い and add ～かったです / ～くなかったです. Here たのしい → たのしかったです and むずかしい → むずかしくなかったです.

french.title: Aller ou être hier
french.objective: Distinguez un déplacement accompli avec être allé d’un état ou jugement passé avec a été, et accordez allé avec le sujet.
french.focus: aller: être + allé(e)(s); être: avoir + été

spanish.title: Past routines with the imperfect
spanish.objective: Past routines with the imperfect: Use the imperfect for past habits or background: estudiaba, comía, vivía.

japanese.title: An old habit and one event
japanese.focus: Japanese does not need a separate form for “used to.” Use よく or いつも with past forms for habits, and a specific time for a single event.

french.title: Avant et maintenant
french.objective: Décrivez d’anciennes habitudes et situations à l’imparfait, puis opposez-les à la vie actuelle au présent.
french.focus: imparfait: -ais/-ait/-ions/-iez/-aient; avoir → avait; maintenant + présent

spanish.title: Por and para: first contrasts
spanish.objective: Por and para: first contrasts: Para often marks purpose, recipient or destination.

japanese.title: Purpose and reason
japanese.focus: Purpose can use a verb’s ます-stem + に いきます (べんきょうします → べんきょうしに) or noun + の ために. Reason can use ～から or ～ので.

french.title: Pour, par et vers
french.objective: Choisissez pour pour un bénéficiaire ou un but, par pour un passage ou une cause, et vers pour une direction.
french.focus: pour + bénéficiaire/infinitif; par + passage/cause; vers + direction

spanish.title: Connect ideas and review
spanish.objective: Connect ideas and review: Y adds an idea, pero contrasts it, porque explains a reason, and entonces signals a result or next step.

japanese.title: Connect and review ideas
japanese.focus: そして adds, でも contrasts, それから sequences, and だから gives a result. でかける is the plain form of でかけます before よてい. Make a short coherent account and review particles and polite forms.

french.title: Relier ses idées
french.objective: Reliez une idée supplémentaire, une opposition, une raison et une conséquence avec et, mais, parce que et donc/alors.
french.focus: et; mais; parce que; donc/alors; puis/ensuite

spanish.title: Introduce a classmate
spanish.objective: Introduce a classmate: Say each Spanish vowel clearly: a, e, i, o, u.

japanese.title: Introduce a classmate to the study group
japanese.focus: Introduce a new group member, ask about a preference, recall a meeting with polite past ～ました, make a plan with ～つもりです, and describe how studying went with an い-adjective past (たのしい → たのしかったです).

french.title: Présenter une nouvelle camarade au groupe
french.objective: Introduce a new classmate to a group, adapt tu/vous and role information, and answer two follow-up questions without prompts.
french.focus: présenter quelqu’un; tu/vous; venir de; parce que; reformulation polie

spanish.title: Pack for a first class
spanish.objective: Pack for a first class: A noun has grammatical gender.

japanese.title: Pack for the first class
japanese.focus: Read a supplies note, count items, and clarify which things are needed. Bound notebooks use ～さつ: にさつ means two notebooks. The polite request is ～てください: もつ becomes もって, くる becomes きて, so もってきてください means “please bring.”

french.title: Adapter une liste de matériel
french.objective: Read a short supplies brief, reconcile what is already available with what is missing, and explain a revised packing list.
french.focus: il faut; il manque; avoir besoin de; à la place de; confirmation explicite

spanish.title: Prepare materials for a group
spanish.objective: Prepare materials for a group: Usually add -s after a vowel and -es after a consonant.

japanese.title: Prepare for a small group
japanese.focus: Coordinate quantities, recipients, and materials; confirm what each person received. Count bound notebooks with ～さつ (さんさつ, いっさつ); general ～つ works for pens here.

french.title: Répartir le matériel entre quatre personnes
french.objective: Count and allocate shared materials to named recipients, explain a shortage, and agree who will bring the missing items.
french.focus: il manque; il nous faut; chacun; lui/leur; proposer une répartition équitable

spanish.title: Identity or current condition?
spanish.objective: Identity or current condition?: Use ser for identity, origin and characteristics.

japanese.title: Identity, condition, and location
japanese.focus: Separate who someone is, how they feel, and where they are. つかれています describes a resulting state (“is tired”), not an action in progress.

french.title: Préciser un rôle et un état passager
french.objective: Distinguish a person’s role from a temporary condition, ask a clarification question and restate the confirmed facts.
french.focus: être responsable de; être disponible; se sentir; sembler; demander qui et quand

spanish.title: Describe a room accurately
spanish.objective: Describe a room accurately: Hay means there is or there are.

japanese.title: Describe a room accurately
japanese.focus: Distinguish people and objects with います/あります and give useful locations. ついています describes the resulting state of a light being on.

french.title: Signaler ce qui a changé dans une salle
french.objective: Describe a room from two observations, distinguish people from objects, and explain what moved or is missing.
french.focus: il y avait / il y a; se trouver; être dans/sur/sous; déplacer; manquer

spanish.title: Ask instead of guessing
spanish.objective: Ask instead of guessing: Put no before the verb to make a negative.

japanese.title: Clarify the route to a meeting
japanese.focus: Confirm tomorrow’s meeting place and time, then say you do not know the route. Use a map, ask a follow-up question, and check whether you can get there alone. In この みちを いきます, を marks the road you travel along.

french.title: Corriger une demande mal comprise
french.objective: Recognize a misunderstood request, reformulate it politely, check the answer and summarize the agreement.
french.focus: pardon; pourriez-vous répéter; je voulais dire; si je comprends bien; confirmer

spanish.title: Explain your study routine
spanish.objective: Explain your study routine: Remove -ar and add -o, -as, -a, -amos, -an: hablo, hablas, habla, hablamos, hablan.

japanese.title: Explain how you study a difficult word
japanese.focus: Ask どうやって ('how') and explain a repeatable study strategy rather than only listing a daily schedule. Use ききます for asking a teacher, やりかた for a method, and すこしずつ for gradual progress. Reuse polite question-and-answer turns.

french.title: Adapter son programme d’étude
french.objective: Describe a weekly study routine, contrast it with today’s exception and agree on a revised schedule.
french.focus: imparfait habituel; présent exceptionnel; sauf; au lieu de; proposer un autre créneau

spanish.title: Read and write a short message
spanish.objective: Read and write a short message: Remove -ir and add -o, -es, -e, -imos, -en.
spanish.focus: Read and write a short message

japanese.title: Reply to a short message
japanese.focus: Read a plan, reply with a time and place, and confirm the meeting. In a written reply, put the exact words inside 「」 and add と after the closing quote: 「…」と かきました / かえしました means “wrote … / replied ….”

french.title: Lire un message et négocier un rendez-vous
french.objective: Extract a request and deadline from a message, write a concise reply, and confirm a new meeting time.
french.focus: repérer demande et échéance; demander de; répondre que; conditionnel poli; convenir de

spanish.title: Choose and describe an item
spanish.objective: Choose and describe an item: Adjectives agree with the noun they describe: un libro rojo, unas mochilas rojas.

japanese.title: Choose an item and explain why
japanese.focus: Use demonstratives and adjectives to compare two items and make a choice. さんぜん has a sound change from せん; どちら means which of two here.

french.title: Comparer des options et justifier son choix
french.objective: Compare two candidate items using relevant properties, give a reason for the choice and check the other person’s preference.
french.focus: plus/moins/aussi...que; meilleur; cependant; vérifier la préférence

spanish.title: Return the right belongings
spanish.objective: Return the right belongings: Possessives agree with what is possessed, not the owner: mi libro, mis libros; tu mesa, tus mesas.

japanese.title: Return the right belongings
japanese.focus: Identify ownership, describe an item, and return it politely. Link two actions in order with the て-form: みる becomes みて, so かさを みて、うなずきます means “look at the umbrella and nod.”

french.title: Retrouver le propriétaire d’un objet
french.objective: Identify an owner from several clues, describe the item precisely and return it while confirming its ownership.
french.focus: possessifs; celui/celle; le/la/les; appartenir à; demander confirmation

spanish.title: Order around different preferences
spanish.objective: Order around different preferences: With gustar, the liked thing controls the verb: me gusta el libro; me gustan los libros.

japanese.title: Order for two people
japanese.focus: Ask preferences, order for two, and confirm an ingredient that someone does not want. For an ingredient in a dish, はいる becomes はいって. はいっています means “is in it / contains” (a present state), and the negative はいっていません means “is not in it / does not contain it.” This is a present state, not a past event.

french.title: Commander pour deux personnes
french.objective: Ask about two people’s preferences and a restriction, place an order and confirm that each person receives the right item.
french.focus: aimer/préférer; sans; au lieu de; lui/leur; confirmer chaque commande

spanish.title: Make a plan everyone can do
spanish.objective: Make a plan everyone can do: Poder changes o to ue except in nosotros: puedo, puedes, puede, podemos, pueden.
spanish.focus: Make a plan everyone can do

japanese.title: Make a plan both can do
japanese.focus: Negotiate ability, permission, and timing before agreeing on a plan. ～なら sets a condition: さんじなら means “if it is at three.”

french.title: Négocier un projet de groupe réalisable
french.objective: Combine ability, permission, location and timing to propose a plan that everyone can follow.
french.focus: pouvoir; devoir; si + présent; d’abord/ensuite; vérifier permissions et horaires

spanish.title: Explain what needs doing
spanish.objective: Explain what needs doing: Necesitar + infinitive expresses a need.

japanese.title: Explain what needs doing
japanese.focus: Give a short task list, separate must-do from optional actions, and confirm completion.

french.title: Transformer une demande en tâches prioritaires
french.objective: Read a short request, distinguish required from optional tasks, assign responsibility and confirm completion criteria.
french.focus: il faut; devoir; avant de; nécessaire/facultatif; responsabilité et critère de fin

spanish.title: Tell a daily routine in order
spanish.objective: Tell a daily routine in order: A reflexive pronoun changes with the person: me, te, se, nos, se.
spanish.focus: Tell a daily routine in order

japanese.title: Tell a daily routine and a changed plan
japanese.focus: ふだん marks the usual pattern and きょう marks today's change. Order actions with まず, それから, and さいごに. Use polite ～ます for the usual routine, ～ています for the ongoing train delay, and ～ました/～ていました for the completed arrival and waiting.

french.title: Raconter une habitude et son interruption
french.objective: Describe a normal sequence, then explain a specific interruption and the next action.
french.focus: imparfait de routine; soudain; passé composé de rupture; d’abord/ensuite

spanish.title: Give directions on campus
spanish.objective: Give directions on campus: Use en for in/on/at as context requires.

japanese.title: Give directions and verify
japanese.focus: Use destinations, action locations, and position nouns to guide someone and check understanding.

french.title: Guider vers une entrée de remplacement
french.objective: Give multi-step directions using landmarks, ask the listener to repeat the route and correct a wrong turn.
french.focus: tourner; traverser; à côté de; si...alors; vérification par reformulation

spanish.title: Separate now from tomorrow
spanish.objective: Separate now from tomorrow: Use a present form of ir + a + infinitive: voy a estudiar.

japanese.title: Now versus tomorrow
japanese.focus: Contrast an action happening now with an intention or scheduled future action. まだ きめていません means “have not decided yet”: まだ + ～ていません says something has not happened so far (compare きめませんでした, “did not decide”). It is the same ～ていません form first practiced with はいっていません in Master 11.

french.title: Distinguer le travail en cours du plan de demain
french.objective: Report what is happening now, state a near-future intention and explain what must finish first.
french.focus: être en train de; aller + infinitif; avant de; conséquence sur un plan proche

spanish.title: Refer back without repeating
spanish.objective: Refer back without repeating: Lo, la, los and las replace a direct object and agree with it: el libro → lo; las llaves → las.

japanese.title: Refer back naturally
japanese.focus: Use context to avoid repeating clear objects; ask when an omitted reference is not clear.

french.title: Réparer une référence ambiguë
french.objective: Track two people and several objects across turns, use unambiguous references and repair a pronoun misunderstanding.
french.focus: le/la/les; lui/leur; celui-ci/celle-là; reformulation explicite

spanish.title: Tell what happened yesterday
spanish.objective: Tell what happened yesterday: The preterite reports completed past actions.

japanese.title: Tell yesterday's outing
japanese.focus: Narrate several completed actions in polite past, then check one detail with a partner.

french.title: Raconter une sortie passée dans l’ordre
french.objective: Narrate a completed outing in time order, include who went where and what happened, then answer follow-up questions.
french.focus: passé composé avec avoir/être; d’abord/puis/finalement; cause et ordre

spanish.title: Contrast a habit and an event
spanish.objective: Contrast a habit and an event: Use the imperfect for past habits or background: estudiaba, comía, vivía.
spanish.focus: Contrast a habit and an event

japanese.title: A habit versus one event
japanese.focus: Contrast what often happened with one dated event; use time words rather than inventing an imperfect tense.

french.title: Expliquer comment une habitude a changé
french.objective: Explain what usually happened before, what happened once, and how the one event affected the routine.
french.focus: imparfait habituel; passé composé ponctuel; depuis; cause et conséquence

spanish.title: Spanish 101 final conversation
spanish.objective: Spanish 101 final conversation: Y adds an idea, pero contrasts it, porque explains a reason, and entonces signals a result or next step.

japanese.title: A full everyday conversation
japanese.focus: Greet, clarify a word, plan a meeting, refer back to a previous visit, and close a short conversation politely. いってください can mean “please say” (言って) here; the same kana means “please go” (行って) in Master 15. Context identifies the verb.

french.title: Mener une conversation complète en français
french.objective: Open, clarify, compare, decide, report a past event and close a conversation with minimal prompting and suitable register.
french.focus: ouvrir; clarifier; comparer; négocier; événement passé; récapituler; tu/vous
